rationale: Cortical visual impairment (CVI) is confirmed in the literature as a recurrent but minority feature of MAPK8IP3-related neurodevelopmental disorder (NEDBA). In the seminal defining cohort by Platzer et al. (2019), CVI was documented in 2 of 13 individuals (15.4%), specifically clustering in patients harboring the recurrent de novo missense variant p.Arg1146Cys. Later literature, clinical registries, and functional reviews (e.g., Crowder et al., Wolverine Foundation, Zhang et al.) consistently list CVI among the less frequent / minority clinical findings (co-occurring with spasticity and severe brain anomalies) rather than a universal hallmark, distinguishing these retro-axonal transport/neurodevelopmental presentations from primary ocular anterior/optic nerve diseases.

evidence.text: Platzer et al. identified de novo MAPK8IP3 variants in 13 unrelated individuals and noted that cortical visual impairment was specifically present in two individuals carrying the recurrent p.Arg1146Cys missense variant (2/13, 15.4%).

evidence.text: Zhang et al. documented that MAPK8IP3/JIP3 mutations lead to broad neurodevelopmental phenotypes including intellectual disability, motor delay, seizures, and visual impairment, contrasting toxic gain-of-function missense mutations (such as Arg578Cys) with other phenotypes.

new_directions.question_text: Does cortical visual impairment specifically correlate with C-terminal domain missense variants such as p.Arg1146Cys, or does it manifest across truncating and other regional missense variants when assessed systematically using standardized visual evoked potentials and functional ophthalmologic scoring?
new_directions.rationale: In the initial cohort of 13 patients, CVI was restricted specifically to the two individuals harboring p.Arg1146Cys. Expanding formal visual assessments across larger multicenter cohorts with diverse domain mutations will determine if CVI is a domain-specific phenotype or an under-recognized secondary manifestation of generalized cortical malformation/atrophy.
